NOTE — GPA-cum-Sale is NOT valid mode of transferring immovable property (Suraj Lamp v. State of Haryana 2012); GPA does NOT confer ownership. Distinguish from SPA (limited scope).

title: General Power of Attorney (Powers of Attorney Act, 1882)

causeTitle.format:
GENERAL POWER OF ATTORNEY

KNOW ALL MEN BY THESE PRESENTS that I, {grantor_name}, son/daughter/wife of {grantor_father_name}, aged about {grantor_age} years, resident of {grantor_address}, (PAN: {grantor_pan}, Aadhaar last 4: {grantor_aadhaar_last4})
(hereinafter referred to as the "GRANTOR" / "PRINCIPAL")

do hereby nominate, constitute and appoint:

{attorney_name}, son/daughter/wife of {attorney_father_name}, aged about {attorney_age} years, resident of {attorney_address}, (PAN: {attorney_pan}, Aadhaar last 4: {attorney_aadhaar_last4})
(hereinafter referred to as the "ATTORNEY" / "AGENT")

as my true and lawful Attorney to act in my name and on my behalf in respect of the matters specified hereinafter.

promptInstructions: Draft a GENERAL POWER OF ATTORNEY under the Powers-of-Attorney Act, 1882 read with Indian Contract Act, 1872 (Chapter X — Agency, S.182-238).
Powers of Attorney Act, 1882, S.1A — defines 'Power of Attorney' as any instrument empowering a specified person to act for and in the name of the person executing it.
S.2 — Execution under power of attorney is execution in name of principal; binding on principal.

CRITICAL — Suraj Lamp & Industries Pvt Ltd v. State of Haryana (2012) 1 SCC 656: GPA-cum-Sale or 'SA-cum-GPA-cum-Will' transactions are NOT valid modes of transfer of immovable property. A GPA, even if it includes power to sell, does NOT itself transfer title. Title can only pass by a registered sale deed. The Supreme Court has SPECIFICALLY held that such GPA-cum-sale shortcuts are an evasion of stamp duty + registration + tax law and not legally effective for transfer of ownership.

If user data shows GPA includes power to sell immovable property — MUST insert a prominent disclaimer in the deed: 'This GPA confers powers of management and representation. It does NOT operate as a transfer of ownership of any immovable property. Any sale of immovable property covered hereby shall be effected only by a duly stamped and registered Sale Deed. The Grantor's title shall stand transferred ONLY upon registration of such Sale Deed.'
DISTINGUISH FROM SPA: SPA (Special Power of Attorney) is for a SPECIFIC transaction (e.g., 'to execute sale deed of plot X to buyer Y at consideration Z'). GPA is broader.
STRUCTURE:
Para 1: Preamble — 'Know all men by these presents that I, [Grantor], aged [age], resident of [address], do hereby...'
Para 2: Recital of reason — grantor abroad / NRI / ill / employed elsewhere / unable to personally attend; brief, factual.
Para 3: Appointment — 'I hereby nominate, constitute and appoint [Attorney name + identification + relationship] as my true and lawful Attorney to do the following acts in my name and on my behalf'.

Para 4: ENUMERATED POWERS — be specific. Vague 'do all acts' clauses fail S.202 ICA and are construed narrowly. Common heads:
   (a) Property management — receive rent, pay outgoings, repair, mutate records.
   (b) Leasing — negotiate, execute and register lease agreements up to 11 months; for longer leases, [include / exclude] authority.
   (c) Sale negotiation (NOT title transfer) — negotiate, agree price; signing of sale deed only with grantor's specific consent in writing.
   (d) Bank operations — operate specified bank account, deposit, withdraw, sign cheques; specify account number to avoid open mandate.
   (e) Tax — file income tax returns, GST returns, property tax; sign on grantor's behalf; receive refunds.
   (f) Government authorities — appear before Registrar, Sub-Registrar, Tehsildar, Municipal Corporation, RTO, etc.
   (g) Litigation — engage advocates, sign vakalatnamas, pleadings, affidavits, swear / verify on oath; receive sums awarded in favour of grantor.
   (h) Substitution — power to appoint sub-attorney (avoid unless trust verified; default — no substitution).
   (i) Contracts — execute service / supply / sale of goods contracts up to specified value.
   (j) Business interest — represent grantor's partnership / shareholding (specify entity, scope of authority).

Para 5: LIMITATIONS — explicitly state what attorney CANNOT do:
   - Cannot make a WILL on grantor's behalf (will is non-delegable; S.59 ISA — testator must himself sign).
   - Cannot GIFT grantor's property to self or family of attorney.
   - Cannot create any encumbrance benefiting attorney personally.
   - Cannot waive grantor's vested rights without specific instruction.
   - Cannot represent grantor in any matter where attorney has personal interest adverse to grantor.
Para 6: RATIFICATION — 'I hereby ratify all and singular the lawful acts performed by my said Attorney within the scope of authority herein granted'.
Para 7: FIDUCIARY DUTY / NO SELF-DEALING — attorney is fiduciary; cannot transact for personal benefit; must keep accounts.
Para 8: DURATION — until revoked / fixed term / until specified event (e.g., grantor's return to India).

Para 9: REVOCATION — grantor may revoke at any time by written notice (unless irrevocable under S.202 Contract Act — i.e., where attorney has acquired interest in subject matter — rare). On revocation, attorney must hand over all documents and accounts.
Para 10: TERMINATION on death of grantor (per S.201 ICA), insolvency, insanity.
Para 11: INDEMNITY — attorney indemnifies grantor for losses arising from unauthorised acts.

Para 12: STAMP DUTY — state-specific (verify):
   - Bihar: Article 48 Bihar Stamp Schedule — Rs.100 to higher amounts depending on type.
   - Jharkhand: similar.
   - UP: Article 48 — Rs.10 to Rs.100 for general; higher where GPA authorises sale of immovable.
   - Delhi: Article 48 Delhi Stamp Schedule — varies; for sale authorisation, higher duty applicable.

Para 13: AUTHENTICATION:
   (a) Notarisation — minimum requirement under Notaries Act, 1952.
   (b) Registration under S.17(1) Registration Act — NOT mandatory for ordinary GPA, BUT mandatory for GPA executed by NRIs OR for GPAs that include power to sell immovable property (per state amendments and Suraj Lamp directives). Several states (Delhi, Haryana, UP) have circulars requiring registration for property GPAs.
   (c) GPA executed abroad — must be (i) attested by Indian Consulate / Embassy OR (ii) apostilled (if grantor in Hague Apostille Convention country) AND (iii) authenticated under S.18 Registration Act within 3 months of arrival in India.
Para 14: WITNESSES — two adult attesting witnesses (mandatory under Notaries Act / Registration Act).
Para 15: Where Grantor is a company — Board Resolution authorising execution annexed; signed by Authorised Signatory.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

filing_checklist: Stamp paper of correct denomination (state Article 48)
Grantor's Identity / Address proof — PAN + Aadhaar / Passport
Attorney's Identity / Address proof — PAN + Aadhaar / Passport
Two passport-size photographs of grantor and attorney
Two adult witnesses with own ID proofs
REGISTRATION at Sub-Registrar if GPA includes power to sell immovable OR per state-specific requirements
If grantor abroad: Consular attestation by Indian Embassy / Consulate OR Apostille (Hague Convention countries); must be authenticated under S.18 Registration Act within 3 months of arrival in India
If company is grantor: Board Resolution authorising GPA + Memorandum of Association extract
Where GPA authorises operation of bank accounts: bank-specific mandate forms in addition (banks accept GPA but follow KYC)
Where GPA authorises court representation: vakalatnama in advocate's favour to be filed separately when needed
Photographs of Grantor and Attorney affixed and signed across
WARNING — Suraj Lamp v. State of Haryana (2012) 1 SCC 656: GPA does NOT transfer title to immovable property. Any sale must be by registered Sale Deed.
